speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're having trouble walking and feeling pain in a specific area, but you feel generally well and have no fever. To narrow down the cause, can you point to the exact spot where it hurts the most, and does the pain get worse when you put weight on that leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis (likely, given age, pain location, and lack of trauma/fever, though Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis must be ruled out given the chronic nature of limp; further imaging is required). I will order imaging to confirm. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, ESR, CRP. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Left Hip and Knee.
